haiku-low.q1: A PR check builds the image locally without pushing, then runs unit tests; it never deploys. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging, production and the canary deploy the same image, tagged with the merge SHA. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure: one automatic whole-suite retry; if it fails again, the run ends and unit tests are cancelled. Unit failure: no retry, run ends, integration tests cancelled.
haiku-low.q4: Staging is rolled back to the previous_tag image. deploy.sh rollback staging reads it from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag and sets the image.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers members who are not commit authors may approve. No approval within 72 hours expires the run; nothing reaches production.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful stable rollout; the canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Canary-off removes canary traffic and stable is untouched. Tags are not written. The migration stays applied, since migrations are never undone.
haiku-low.q8: It stops as superseded, not a failure: no production deploy, and a one-line note is posted in #deploys.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it waits for the next Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC opening, exempt from the 72-hour expiry. Lock contention behaviour: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: Canary 5xx ratio, sampled every 30 s for 15 minutes. Fails above 1% on any sample, or after 3 no-data samples in a row.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for how approvers are notified. The gate is a manual CI approval job that records approver and time. Decision information: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: Neither gets automatic rollback; on-call decides in production. Rollback would set previous_tag, which is wrong after a failed rollout, so it is avoided.

sonnet.q1: A PR runs the PR check: builds the image locally (no push) and runs unit tests; it never pushes or deploys. A merge to main starts the run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the single image built once per merge, tagged with the full SHA and pushed to registry.internal/shop-api (canary uses the same tag). Nothing is rebuilt after the tests; reruns reuse the pushed image.
sonnet.q3: Unit test failure: no retry, run fails immediately, integration suite cancelled, announced in #deploys. Integration failure: the whole suite is retried once automatically; if it fails again the run fails, unit tests are cancelled, announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q4: The pipeline runs deploy.sh rollback staging, which reads previous_tag from SSM, sets the stable image to it and writes current_tag. So staging runs the previous tag (previous_tag), found in SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag. The run fails and is announced; the staging-deploy lock is held through the rollback.
sonnet.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, and not an author of the merged commit (such an approval is rejected by a check step and the gate stays open). If no approval within 72 h of the gate opening, the run expires, is announced in #deploys, and nothing reaches production.
sonnet.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful rollout (previous_tag first, then current_tag; also current_tag on rollback). The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment is untouched (canary-off runs, canary scaled back to 0). SSM tags are unchanged since the canary writes nothing. The database schema keeps the migration, since migrations are forward-only and never undone; it is safe because every migration must work with the previous image.
sonnet.q8: The older run is superseded: when approved and at production start, the check that staging still runs its SHA fails, so there is no production deploy. It is not a failure or alert; a one-line note goes to #deploys.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it waits for the next window opening (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) and is not subject to the 72 h expiry. While another production deploy is in progress: NOT STATED (the prod-deploy lock allows only one at a time, but the document does not say whether the run waits or fails).
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio (share of canary requests with 5xx over the last minute) from Prometheus, using the stated query. The pipeline's watch step samples every 30 s for 15 min, starting after the canary rollout is ready. Failure: any sample above 1 percent, or 3 consecutive samples with no data.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how approvers are notified that a run is waiting. The document only says approvers get a one-line note in #deploys when a run is superseded; the gate opens after staging smoke tests pass, and CI records who approved and when. What information they decide with is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q12: It is not automatically rolled back in either case. Staging: run fails, tags unchanged, no rollback. Production: tags not written, no rollback, prod-deploy lock kept, on-call decides. Reason: a failed rollout leaves current_tag unchanged, so deploy.sh rollback would set the image to previous_tag, which does not name what was running (wrong tag). The document does not say how the environment is returned to a known image afterward (staging: NOT STATED; production: on-call decides).
